IF YOU'RE ADDING A NEW TRACK...

Make sure the costume name is called "track" followed by the number above the one from previous costume. If you want to make a retro track, those start at 25.

The race always starts at the center of the costume pointing up.

To make alternating costumes, go to the "set costume" custom block in the sprite you want the costumes to alternate in, then add an if loop with your track ID and the checkpoint ID the costume should switch after.

Don't base coordinates on mirror or reverse mode!

Don't forget to add: (* is required, - is optional)
* the main road (in this sprite)
- the offroad areas (in "Mud")
- walls and solid obstacles (in "Walls")
- one-way walls (in "Semi-Solids", direction allowed is the direction of the last checkpoint passed)
* checkpoints (in the scripts area of "checkpoints")
* item boxes (in "item boxes", works like checkpoints, 3 locations per course)
* coins (in "coins", works like checkpoints, exactly 8 per course)
- speed pads (in "speed pads", works like checkpoints)
* the background (in the backdrops area of the stage)
* the music (in the sounds area of the stage: you need to separate the intro, which is the part of the song you hear at the beginning that doesn't repeat, and the loop, which is the part of the song that repeats or "loops" throughout the majority of the track.)
* CPU training (all you have to do is complete one lap! See the CPUData sprite for instructions)
* Points of interest for Grand Prix track preview (press the 1 and 2 keys in debug mode)

IF YOU'RE ADDING A NEW BATTLE ARENA...

Do the same as if you were adding a regular race track, but make the number after "track" negative.

IF YOU'RE DOING ANYTHING ELSE...
Remember to never "clean up" the scripts.

-NEW INFORMATION! How to add item boxes:

Adding item boxes used to involve painstakingly copying numbers from the debug screen. Not anymore! Press Q to access the all-new track editor, which lets you place all coordinate-based objects via the intuitive mouse-based editor. (You can even press Q outside of a race -- this lets you switch between tracks really quickly!) Unlike the old way of doing things, the item boxes will now instantaneously update after adding.

If you need to edit or delete an item box, go to the Editor sprite (at the bottom of the sprites list) for further instructions.

Don't worry about remaking item boxes for mirror or reverse variations of tracks. The game will convert them for you.

-Revised Guidelines (IMPORTANT):

Make sure to place multiple item boxes across the width of the track to ensure that there's enough for everyone and that it's hard to not drive through one. In general, 2-4 is a good guideline, although this will vary.

THERE SHOULD BE EXACTLY 3 LOCATIONS ON THE COURSE WITH ITEM BOXES. Every single course in Mario Kart 8 follows this trend. They should be relatively spaced out to allow time for drivers to use the items before arriving at the next set of boxes.

+.hJ?;Zdpg$PuGy)j2D1.text:
-NEW INFORMATION! How to add coins:

Adding coins used to involve painstakingly copying numbers from the debug screen. Not anymore! Press Q to access the all-new track editor, which lets you place all coordinate-based objects via the intuitive mouse-based editor. (You can even press Q outside of a race -- this lets you switch between tracks really quickly!) Unlike the old way of doing things, the coins will now instantaneously update after adding.

If you need to edit or delete a coin, go to the Editor sprite (at the bottom of the sprites list) for further instructions.

Don't worry about remaking coins for mirror or reverse variations of tracks. The game will convert them for you.

-Revised Guidelines (IMPORTANT):

You rarely want coins to be in a convenient location: that being said, you don't want the player to go off-road in order to get them. The most common method is to place them on the outside edge of a corner (not off-road) so that the player needs to choose between taking the shorter path or collecting the coin. However, you could also make them a fun mini-challenge for the driver: for example, placing them on a tricky pathway or scattering them around a glider section.

As per current design conventions, YOU SHOULD PLACE EXACTLY 8 COINS PER COURSE. Use them wisely!

-NEW INFORMATION! How to add glider/boost pads:

Adding boost pads used to involve painstakingly copying numbers from the debug screen. Not anymore! Press Q to access the all-new track editor, which lets you place all coordinate-based objects via the intuitive mouse-based editor. (You can even press Q outside of a race -- this lets you switch between tracks really quickly!) Unlike the old way of doing things, the checkpoints will now instantaneously update after adding.

If you need to edit or delete a boost pad, go to the Editor sprite (at the bottom of the sprites list) for further instructions.

Unlike everything else, you SHOULD consider the reverse variant of boost pads when there are big gaps that can only be cleared with said boost pads. You can make boost pads only appear in reverse mode (or regular mode) via a setting accessed right before you place them.

-Revised Guidelines (IMPORTANT):

If you're creating a course that already exists in Mario Kart 8 or another game, try your best to place the boost pads the same way they were in the original track. It doesn't have to be perfect, it's just a consistency thing.

YOU MUST TEST GLIDER SECTIONS AT 50CC in order to ensure that the player can easily clear the jump with room to spare. If the jump is too big, try adding a boost pad before the glider pad and giving the player more room to accelerate -- especially after respawning.

-NEW INFORMATION! How to add checkpoints:

Adding checkpoints used to involve painstakingly copying numbers from the debug screen. Not anymore! Press Q to access the all-new track editor, which lets you place all coordinate-based objects via the intuitive mouse-based editor. (You can even press Q outside of a race -- this lets you switch between tracks really quickly!) Unlike the old way of doing things, the checkpoints will now instantaneously update after adding.

If you need to edit or delete a checkpoint, go to the Editor sprite (at the bottom of the sprites list) for further instructions.

Don't worry about remaking checkpoints for mirror or reverse variations of tracks. The game will convert them for you.

-Revised Guidelines (IMPORTANT):

When visible, each checkpoint should go up a color of the rainbow further through the track. Make sure the order of the checkpoints is correct! You can also view the number order of any given checkpoint by hovering over it with the mouse-pointer.

Make sure it isn't possible to drive past checkpoints and/or drive through checkpoints in the wrong order, or else the lap might not count. You can add walls to the sides of the checkpoint, change the checkpoint's size, or place it somewhere else to ensure this.

YOU MUST HAVE AT LEAST 3 CHECKPOINTS FOR LAPS TO WORK. Checkpoints should be relatively close to each other (use MK Stadium for reference). At the very least, place checkpoints throughout and/or after curves so that Lakitu correctly tracks your location. Checkpoints are also used for respawning (and place determination), so it's especially important to place them before places where the player can drive off the track. (If the track has few walls, lots of checkpoints would be a good idea.)

Make sure the arrow on the checkpoints point in the direction you're supposed to drive in. Unless you want to annoy people by respawning the player backwards.
